glossary.title: Dimensions and Tags Glossary
glossary.description: This glossary explains each analytical dimension and its respective tags used in mapping political thinkers.
glossary.tip: Use the filters at the top of the page to explore thinkers by any combination of these dimensions.

tag_descriptions.freedom: Emphasis on individual autonomy and limitation of state power.
tag_descriptions.authority: Valuing order, hierarchy, and legitimacy of central power.
tag_descriptions.state: Defense of an active and regulatory role of the State in the economy and society.
tag_descriptions.market: Trust in free market mechanisms and economic competition.
tag_descriptions.community: Focus on forms of community organization and local solidarity.
tag_descriptions.tradition: Preservation of established values, institutions, and practices.
tag_descriptions.rupture: Defense of radical changes and transformation of existing structures.
tag_descriptions.individual: Prioritization of the rights and interests of the individual.
tag_descriptions.collective: Emphasis on the interests of the group, class, or nation.
tag_descriptions.rationalist: Grounding in deductive reasoning and universal a priori principles, independently of experience.
tag_descriptions.empiricist: Grounding in observation, concrete experience, and real-world data as the basis of political knowledge.
tag_descriptions.idealist: Primacy of ideas, values, consciousness, and norms as the driving forces of political reality.
tag_descriptions.materialist: Primacy of material interests, power relations, and concrete structures as the driving forces of political reality.
tag_descriptions.interactionist: Simultaneous recognition of ideal and material forces as drivers of political reality, whose interaction is the very explanatory object — without subordinating one pole to the other. (E.g.: Tocqueville, Weber, Aristotle, Arendt)
tag_descriptions.ahistorical: Pursuit of timeless, universal political principles valid independently of historical context.
tag_descriptions.historicist: Understanding political phenomena through their historical evolution and determination, without positing a universal law of motion.
tag_descriptions.dialectical: History moves through necessary internal contradictions that produce syntheses — transformation is immanent to the very structure of reality.
tag_descriptions.optimistic: Positive view of human nature and capacity for progress.
tag_descriptions.pessimistic: Distrust of human nature and need for control.
tag_descriptions.ambivalent: Balanced perspective on human nature: simultaneously recognizes the potentials and the inherent limits of human beings, without resolving the tension toward either pole. (E.g.: Aristotle, Tocqueville, Arendt)
tag_descriptions.universalist: Principles applicable to all humanity, regardless of context.
tag_descriptions.particularist: Valuing specific contexts, cultures, and local traditions.

diagnostic.tendency_freedom: liberal tendency and appreciation of individual autonomy
diagnostic.tendency_authority: inclination toward established order and authority
diagnostic.tradition_value: respect for tradition and gradual change
diagnostic.individual_focus: focus on the individual as the political unit
diagnostic.collective_focus: emphasis on the collective and common good
diagnostic.epistemology_rationalist: rationalist orientation grounded in deductive reasoning and universal a priori principles
diagnostic.epistemology_empiricist: empiricist orientation anchored in observation and concrete experience
diagnostic.ontology_idealist: primacy of ideas and values as the explanatory driver of politics
diagnostic.ontology_materialist: emphasis on material forces, concrete interests, and power relations
diagnostic.ontology_interactionist: interactionist perspective — ideal and material forces as simultaneous drivers
diagnostic.historicity_ahistorical: pursuit of timeless and universal principles independent of historical context
diagnostic.historicity_dialectical: dialectical vision of historical transformation through contradictions and syntheses
